content: Polysorbate 20, also known commercially as Tween 20, is a surfactant that is widely used due to its stability and relatively low toxicity. It functions as both a detergent and an emulsifier in various domestic, scientific, and pharmacological applications. Chemically, it is a polyoxyethylene derivative of sorbitan monolaurate. It is differentiated from other members of the Tween family by the length of its polyoxyethylene chain and the specific fatty acid ester moiety it contains. The commercial product is not a single compound but rather a mixture of related chemical species. Food Applications Polysorbate 20 is utilized as a wetting agent in flavored mouth drops, such as Ice Drops. It enhances the spreading sensation of other ingredients, including SD alcohol and mint flavor. The World Health Organization (WHO) has established an acceptable daily intake range for polyoxyethylene sorbitan esters, which is 0–25 mg per kilogram of body weight. Biological Applications In the field of biological sciences, Polysorbate 20 has a wide array of uses: It serves as a blocking agent in immunoassays, such as Western blotting and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs), to prevent nonspecific binding. It acts as a solubilizing agent for membrane proteins, aiding in their extraction and analysis. It is used for lysing mammalian cells at concentrations ranging from 0.05% to 0.5% (v/v). It can be dissolved in Tris-buffered saline (TBS) or phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) at dilutions of 0.05% to 0.5% (v/v) and is commonly used as a washing solution in immunoassays. Pharmaceutical Applications In pharmaceutical formulations, Polysorbate 20 is employed to stabilize emulsions and suspensions, ensuring the uniform distribution of active ingredients. Industrial and Domestic Applications Polysorbate 20 is also used in industrial and domestic cleaning products. For example, it is listed as a key ingredient in the cleaning solution manufactured by Clorox for the iRobot Scooba floor-washing robot, as indicated on its Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS). Critical Micelle Concentration (CMC) The critical micelle concentration (CMC) of Polysorbate 20 is 8.04 × 10⁻⁵ M at a temperature of 21°C. This value indicates the concentration at which the surfactant molecules begin to form micelles in solution.
